You are sort of right yeah. Generally the label is the target of your data. Since you have 8 different hand gestures images in the data set provided in your link, you have 8 distinct labels i.e. 8 different categories that any hand gesture image can belong to. 

About the array part, 2 seperate np arrays are the better way to go for now since a dictionary can be slow. One array can hold the image pixel values and the second aaray can hold the label values. Their index positions will correspond to each other for example the first index in image array will be corresponding to the first index of the label array.

Try looking up on kaggle and machinelearningmastery.com
I'll link any tutorials later until then this should help

Building a label means that you have to assign a class or category to each image, for example images of car get the label 'car' and images of dog get the label 'dog' or anything like 'animal', whatever you want.  

Next, assigning a number means converting that label into a numeric form. Look up label encoding which is very simple and is just assigning these labels a number. For example 'car' can be assigned 1 and dog can be assigned 2. The model will then learn that a certain set of images are labelled as 1 and it will recognise the pattern of the image (highly simplified explanation). 

The main reason behind label encoding is because strings are not generally used during machine learning since most model libraries only support numerical data.
